labs.name: Aalto Speech Recognition
labs.summary: Speech recognition group at Aalto University, long-term open-source publisher of the Morfessor morphology tool and AaltoASR toolkit.
labs.tagline: Aalto University's speech recognition group, whose open Morfessor and AaltoASR tools have long supported speech and language technology for morphologically rich languages.
about: The speech recognition group sits in the Department of Information and Communications Engineering at Aalto University in Espoo and is part of the Finnish Center for Artificial Intelligence. It works on acoustic modeling of phonemes, statistical language models for large-vocabulary continuous speech recognition, and speech technology for under-resourced languages.

The group publishes its research software through the aalto-speech GitHub organization, created in 2013. The best known repositories are Morfessor, a tool for unsupervised and semi-supervised morphological segmentation, AaltoASR, a set of recognition tools, and speaker diarization scripts built on that toolkit.

Professor Mikko Kurimo heads the group and is known internationally for unsupervised subword modeling for languages with rich word inflection, such as Finnish, Estonian, Turkish and Arabic. The software mainly serves other speech and language researchers.
labs.mission: The group aims to improve speech recognition with new algorithms and to make recognition practical for languages with limited data and heavy inflection. It shares its tools openly so that other researchers can reuse and extend them.

labs.name: AdapterHub
labs.summary: Open-source community and library for parameter-efficient and modular transfer learning, started by researchers around UKP Lab in Darmstadt.
labs.tagline: AdapterHub maintains the open Adapters library, a modular, parameter-efficient fine-tuning toolkit built on Hugging Face Transformers.
about: AdapterHub began in 2020 as a framework for sharing and composing adapters, small sets of added weights that stand in for full fine-tuning of a pretrained model. The original paper by Pfeiffer and colleagues was presented at EMNLP 2020, and the GitHub organization was created in April 2020.

In November 2023 the project released the unified Adapters package, replacing the earlier adapter-transformers fork, with a library paper at EMNLP 2023. The library is released under the Apache 2.0 licence and had about 2,800 GitHub stars in 2026.

Version 1.2.0, announced in May 2025, added a plugin interface for attaching adapter functionality to nearly any Transformer model. The project is run by researchers associated with TU Darmstadt and serves practitioners who need to adapt large models cheaply.
labs.mission: AdapterHub aims to make parameter-efficient and modular transfer learning easy to use, share and combine. It treats adapters as reusable components that the community can publish and compose.

labs.name: Agentica
labs.summary: Open-source initiative from Berkeley's Sky Computing Lab releasing RL-trained models such as DeepScaleR and DeepCoder and the rLLM framework.
labs.tagline: A Berkeley Sky Computing Lab initiative that publishes open reinforcement learning recipes, models and the rLLM framework for training language agents.
about: Agentica is an open-source effort from the Sky Computing Lab at UC Berkeley. It aims to make reinforcement learning techniques for language models and agents widely available, with core contributors Michael Luo and Sijun Tan and a group of student contributors.

The project released DeepScaleR in February 2025, a 1.5B model trained with distributed reinforcement learning for math reasoning. In July 2025 it published DeepCoder, a 14B code reasoning model, the rLLM framework for training agents with reinforcement learning, and DeepSWE, a 32B software engineering agent.
Its advisors are Li Erran Li, Raluca Ada Popa and Ion Stoica. The project site notes that Agentica is becoming a startup named Peano AI.
labs.mission: Agentica states that it wants to democratize reinforcement learning for language models and to build scalable systems for LLMs and agents.

labs.name: AI Singapore
labs.summary: National AI programme (government-funded) behind the SEA-LION family of Southeast Asian language models.
labs.tagline: Singapore's national AI programme, which builds applied AI capability and the open SEA-LION language models for Southeast Asia.
about: AI Singapore was launched in May 2017 as a national initiative that brings together Singapore's research institutions, start-ups and companies. Its work covers applied research, AI governance, innovation support for companies, talent development and open-source AI products.

Among its products is SEA-LION, a family of open language models for Southeast Asian languages and cultures. Reporting describes a first release in 2023 trained on 11 languages, a version 3 built on Llama and Gemma 2, and a version 4 built on Gemma 3 and on Qwen3 with technical support from Alibaba.
The programme also runs talent schemes such as the AI Apprenticeship Programme and offers courses through LearnAI.
labs.mission: AI Singapore states that it aims to strengthen national AI capabilities, build tools and train talent, and to raise Singapore's profile in AI.

labs.summary: Non-profit initiative at IIT Madras building open datasets, models and applications for Indian languages.
labs.tagline: An IIT Madras research lab building open datasets, models and tools for Indian languages in translation, speech and language modelling.
about: AI4Bharat is a research lab at IIT Madras that releases most of its work as open source. Its focus areas are transliteration, language understanding and generation, machine translation, speech recognition and speech synthesis.

Its releases include IndicBERT and IndicBART, the IndicTrans2 translation models covering all 22 scheduled Indian languages and English, speech models such as IndicWav2Vec and IndicWhisper, and datasets including Sangraha and IndicVoices.
IndicVoices, funded by the Bhashini initiative of India's IT ministry, provides about 7,300 hours of speech across 22 languages.
labs.mission: AI4Bharat works to give speakers of Indian languages open language technology comparable to what exists for English.

labs.summary: Artificial Intelligence Laboratory at the Institute of Mathematics and Computer Science, University of Latvia, active since 1992 and building open Latvian language resources such as Tezaurs and FullStack-LV.
labs.tagline: The AI Laboratory at the University of Latvia builds open Latvian language resources, from the Tezaurs lexicon to a multilayer corpus and Latvian BERT models.
about: The Artificial Intelligence Laboratory belongs to the Institute of Mathematics and Computer Science at the University of Latvia in Riga and has conducted research since 1992. Its work covers natural language processing and machine learning, including Latvian speech recognition and synthesis, syntactic and semantic analysis and language models.

The lab maintains a set of public Latvian resources, among them Tezaurs.lv, Korpuss.lv, the LV-PIPE tools, CLARIN-LV and Balsutalka.lv. Its FullStack-LV repository offers a multilayer corpus with Universal Dependencies, FrameNet, PropBank and AMR layers, released under a Creative Commons licence.

Funding comes from the European Union, the European Regional Development Fund and Latvian ministries and councils. The lab has partnered with the news agency LETA, Deutsche Welle and the National Library of Latvia.
labs.mission: The lab states that it develops resources and technologies that help Latvian thrive in a multilingual environment. It publishes its tools and data openly for researchers and developers.

labs.summary: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Lab at TU Darmstadt, open-sourcing safety tooling for vision-language and diffusion models such as LlavaGuard and Safe Latent Diffusion.
labs.tagline: The AI and Machine Learning Lab at TU Darmstadt releases open safety tooling and reasoning research, including LlavaGuard and Safe Latent Diffusion.
about: The AIML Lab at TU Darmstadt is led by Professor Kristian Kersting, who joined the university in 2019 and also co-directs hessian.AI. Its stated aims are advancing statistical learning, probabilistic reasoning and collaborative intelligence, with work in statistical relational AI, generative modeling and trustworthy machine learning.

The lab publishes code on GitHub and models on Hugging Face, where it lists 20 models and 42 datasets. Safety tools include Safe Latent Diffusion, LlavaGuard and QwenGuard, and recent releases cover OlmoLogic reasoning models and the KletterMix German pretraining data.
Its audience is researchers and developers who need open checks for image-text datasets and generative models.
labs.mission: The lab aims to make machines learn about the world rapidly and flexibly, combining logical and probabilistic methods with deep learning. It emphasises trustworthy and safe generative systems.

labs.name: Aleph Alpha
labs.summary: Heidelberg language-model company that publishes part of its research as open weights and datasets alongside commercial products.
labs.tagline: Heidelberg language-model company that built sovereign European models and released part of its research as open weights, now being merged into Cohere.
about: Aleph Alpha was founded in 2019 in Heidelberg by Jonas Andrulis and Samuel Weinbach. It raised a 5.3 million euro seed round in 2020, a further 23 million euros in 2021, and in November 2023 announced a large round led by Schwarz Gruppe and the Dieter Schwarz Foundation.

The company sells specialised sovereign language models and solutions to organisations, and also publishes research code, datasets and models. Its Hugging Face organization carries the Kolibri model, a German and English mixture-of-experts model released in October 2026 under Apache 2.0.

In April 2026 Cohere announced that it would acquire Aleph Alpha, and a definitive merger agreement followed in September 2026. The combined company will operate as Cohere, with Heidelberg kept as a research centre, subject to regulatory approval.
labs.mission: The company says it builds specialised sovereign models that give customers control over their data and adapt to their context. Its open releases support German-language and tokenizer research.
labs.notice: Cohere and Aleph Alpha signed a definitive combination agreement on 16 September 2026. The combined company is to operate as Cohere, with Aleph Alpha's Heidelberg office focused on research. The deal is expected to close later in 2026, subject to regulatory approval.

about: The Alexandra Institute was established in Aarhus in 1999 by business people, researchers and public representatives to link Danish companies with university IT research. It became an approved technological service provider in 2007 and has been owned by the Aarhus University Research Foundation since 2012.

Its open source work is published on GitHub and Hugging Face. DaNLP collected Danish datasets and models for tagging, named entity recognition, sentiment and hate speech detection, with a NoDaLiDa 2021 paper; the repository was archived in March 2025. The ScandEval benchmark, described in arXiv 2304.00906, later grew into EuroEval.
The institute serves Danish companies and public bodies and works on language technology, evaluation and responsible AI.
labs.mission: The institute applies IT research to the needs of Danish business and society and publishes language resources so that Danish remains well supported in AI.

about: The Allen Institute for AI, known as Ai2, was founded in 2014 by Microsoft co-founder Paul Allen. Oren Etzioni led it for nine years until 2022, and Ali Farhadi became CEO in July 2023.

The OLMo models and the Dolma corpus were released in February 2024 with data, code and checkpoints, and the Tulu post-training recipes reached version 3 in November 2024.
labs.mission: Ai2 pursues AI research and engineering for the common good, with open release of the models, data and code behind its work.

about: ALMAnaCH is an Inria team in Paris working on natural language processing and digital humanities. Its members include Benoît Sagot and Djamé Seddah, who are authors of the original CamemBERT paper alongside colleagues from Inria and Sorbonne Université.

CamemBERT, a RoBERTa-based French model released under an MIT licence in 2019, became a widely adopted reference. CamemBERT 2.0 followed in 2024, and CamemBERTa, by Wissam Antoun, Sagot and Seddah, explored data-efficient training. The team's Hugging Face organization lists 92 models and 43 datasets, including biomedical encoders and Gaperon sparse autoencoders.
The models serve researchers, companies and public bodies that need open French and biomedical text processing.

labs.tagline: London-based AI safety organisation that evaluates frontier models for scheming and publishes open evaluation and interpretability work.
about: Apollo Research was founded in 2023 and is led by CEO and co-founder Marius Hobbhahn. Its stated goal is to secure frontier AI systems across development, deployment and governance, with a focus on scheming, where advanced systems covertly pursue misaligned objectives.

In 2023 it presented at the UK AI Safety Summit and advised the Frontier AI Taskforce. In 2024 it tested OpenAI's o1 before release and published early evidence of in-context scheming in frontier models; in 2025 it ran evaluations for major labs and worked with OpenAI on anti-scheming interventions.

In 2026 the organisation became a Public Benefit Corporation, opened a San Francisco office and began building Watcher, an agent monitoring tool. It publishes code on GitHub, including end-to-end sparse dictionary learning.
labs.mission: Apollo aims to reduce the risk of deceptive and misaligned AI through evaluations, interpretability research and governance advice. It works with developers and governments.

labs.summary: AutoML research groups at the Universities of Freiburg and Hannover, creators of auto-sklearn, Auto-PyTorch and SMAC3. The shared automl.org site was closed in August 2026.
labs.tagline: The AutoML groups of Freiburg and Hannover, creators of auto-sklearn, SMAC3 and Auto-PyTorch.
about: The AutoML groups at the University of Freiburg and Leibniz University Hannover were led by Frank Hutter and Marius Lindauer, with Matthias Feurer and Katharina Eggensperger among close collaborators. The GitHub organization dates from 2014.

Their system auto-sklearn began as a competition entry and won the first international AutoML challenge in 2015 to 2016 and the second in 2017 to 2018. The 2015 NeurIPS paper introduced it, and auto-sklearn 2.0 appeared in JMLR in 2022. SMAC3 and Auto-PyTorch extend the work to Bayesian optimisation and deep learning.
In an August 2026 post the group announced the closure of automl.org after a decade. Hutter now leads Prior Labs and Lindauer's Hannover group has broadened beyond AutoML.
labs.mission: The groups aimed to make machine learning accessible by automating model and hyperparameter selection, and released their tools as open source for the community.

about: BigCode was established in September 2022 as an open scientific collaboration on the responsible development of code language models. It is stewarded by Hugging Face and ServiceNow and has drawn more than 1,100 members.

labs.summary: Voice AI company that also publishes open state-space language models such as Rene and Llamba.
labs.tagline: A San Francisco voice AI company founded by the Stanford authors of Mamba-style state-space models, which also releases open Rene and Llamba models.
about: Cartesia was founded in 2023 by Karan Goel, Albert Gu, Arjun Desai and Brandon Yang, researchers who worked on state space models in Chris Re's group at Stanford. Goel serves as chief executive and Gu, a lead author of Mamba and a professor at Carnegie Mellon University, serves as chief scientist.

The company builds real-time voice systems on state-space architectures, which process sequences with a fixed-size state rather than attention over the whole context. It raised a $22 million seed round led by Index Ventures, bringing its total to $27 million, and a $64 million Series A led by Kleiner Perkins in March 2025.

Alongside its commercial speech products, Cartesia publishes open research artifacts on Hugging Face and GitHub. These include the Rene language model and the Llamba family of distilled recurrent models, described in a February 2025 paper that converts Llama models into recurrent form with a small fraction of the usual training data.
labs.mission: Cartesia aims to build real-time, on-device voice AI on state-space model architectures, and shares part of its model research openly.

about: The Center for AI Safety was started in 2022 and is led by Dan Hendrycks as executive and research director, with Oliver Zhang as managing director. Its stated purpose is to reduce societal-scale risks from artificial intelligence, and it organizes its staff into research, cloud and DevOps, projects and operations teams.

CAIS has operated a compute cluster since March 2023 that gives university safety researchers access to large models, and it has run machine learning safety workshops, a Trojan detection competition and a philosophy fellowship. In May 2023 it published the Statement on AI Risk, signed by more than 600 researchers and public figures.

Its research output includes widely used open evaluations. HarmBench standardizes tests of automated red teaming and refusal, WMDP measures hazardous knowledge and evaluates unlearning methods, and Humanity's Last Exam collects expert-written questions to measure frontier capability.
labs.mission: CAIS works to reduce societal-scale risks from AI through technical research, field-building and advocacy.
known_for: WMDP and Humanity's Last Exam benchmarks

labs.summary: AI drug-discovery startup that open-sourced the Chai-1 biomolecular structure model.
labs.tagline: A drug-discovery AI startup that released the open Chai-1 biomolecular structure model.
about: Chai Discovery is a drug-discovery company founded in 2024 by Joshua Meier (chief executive), Jack Dent (president), Matthew McPartlon (chief technology officer) and Jacques Boitreaud. Its team came from OpenAI, Meta FAIR, Stripe and Google X, and it describes its work as predicting and reprogramming interactions between biomolecules.

Chai-1, released on 9 September 2024, predicts structures of proteins, small molecules, DNA and RNA. The company published weights and inference code under Apache 2.0 and reported 77 percent success on PoseBusters against 76 percent for AlphaFold3, with competitive results even when run without multiple sequence alignments.

Chai-2, announced in 2025 for de novo antibody design, is a separate model that sources describe as not openly released. Funding has included a $30 million seed round, a $70 million Series A in August 2025 led by Menlo Ventures and a $130 million Series B reported in January 2026.
labs.mission: Chai aims to let scientists design medicines computationally by predicting and engineering molecular interactions.
labs.notice: Chai-1 is released as open source. Later models such as Chai-2 appear to be proprietary.

about: The Center for Information and Language Processing at LMU Munich hosts a deep NLP group led by Hinrich Schütze, whose GitHub organization dates from 2017. Its work targets low-resource and multilingual language technology.

SimAlign (2020) is a word alignment tool, Glot500 (2023) scales corpora and models to 500 languages, and GlotLID is a language identification model that covered 1665 languages in its first version and over 2,000 labels in v3.0 as of April 2024.

labs.mission: The group aims to extend language technology to many more of the world's languages and to publish the resulting data and models openly.

labs.summary: Centre for Language Resources and Technologies at the University of Ljubljana, which publishes Slovene language models, corpora and tools including the GaMS model family.
labs.tagline: The University of Ljubljana centre that builds Slovene language resources, corpora and the open GaMS generative models.
about: CJVT, the Centre for Language Resources and Technologies, is a research unit of the University of Ljubljana with its organizational base at the Faculty of Computer and Information Science and five other participating faculties. It develops and maintains digital language resources for contemporary Slovene and makes tools available free of charge.

Its resources include the Sloleks morphological lexicon, which invites users to vote on accentuation and pronunciation, the ssj500k training corpus and its successor SUK, and the Tolmac system for translating lectures from Slovene. The centre joined the ELEXIS lexicography network in 2020 and works within a national program on language resources and technologies for Slovene that runs from 2019 to 2027.

The GaMS (Generative Model for Slovene) family began in 2024 with a 1 billion parameter model and has grown to 2B, 9B and 27B releases built on Gemma. A March 2026 preprint presents GaMS3-12B, adapted from Gemma 3 with continual pretraining on about 140 billion tokens and an open OCR pipeline for digitizing older Slovene texts.
labs.mission: CJVT aims to build a long-term infrastructure of Slovene language resources and technology and to keep its tools and data openly available.

about: CKIP, the Chinese Knowledge and Information Processing group, is a cross-institute research team of Academia Sinica's Institute of Information Science and Institute of Linguistics. The group dates itself to 1986 and aims to supply resources and research environments for Chinese natural language processing.

Its outputs include word segmentation, parsing, a sentence structure treebank, the Sinica Corpus, the E-HowNet lexical knowledge base, a Kangxi Dictionary ontology, language models and Chinese embeddings. Current research covers deep learning, knowledge representation, language understanding and knowledge extraction.

CKIP Transformers provides traditional Chinese ALBERT, BERT and GPT-2 models with tools for word segmentation, part-of-speech tagging and named entity recognition, distributed through GitHub, Hugging Face and PyPI under GPL-3.0. Wei-Yun Ma, an associate research fellow, is principal investigator of the lab.

about: The Computational Linguistics and Text Mining Lab at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam is led by Piek Vossen and Antske Fokkens. It has moved from computational lexicology and terminology toward broader work in AI and computational linguistics, with research themes in identity, reference and perspectives, meaning representation, and large language models and interpretability.

Vossen founded the Global WordNet Association in 2000 and presided over it until 2024, and the lab contributes to the Dutch Global Wordnet Grid. It states that it publishes models, software and resources as open source, and also teaches a Language and AI master's program.

MedRoBERTa.nl, introduced in 2021 by Stella Verkijk and Vossen, was pre-trained on nearly 10 million hospital notes from Amsterdam UMC. The lab's Python for Text Analysis course, created in 2016, has over 450 GitHub stars.
labs.mission: The lab combines computational linguistics and text mining and releases its models, software and teaching resources openly.

labs.name: Common Crawl Foundation
labs.summary: Nonprofit that publishes a free, open repository of web crawl data used to train many language models.
labs.tagline: A nonprofit that has published free, open web crawl archives since 2008, forming a foundation dataset for language model research.
about: Common Crawl is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit founded in 2007 by Gil Elbaz, who had earlier co-founded Applied Semantics. Its premise was that web-scale crawl data should be available to researchers who lack the resources to run their own crawling infrastructure.

The foundation publishes monthly crawl archives, each typically containing more than two billion pages, in WARC, WAT and WET formats. It also releases URL and CDXJ indexes and host-level and domain-level web graphs. The data is hosted on Amazon Web Services and can be downloaded free of charge.

A small staff of engineers and researchers maintains the crawler and the datasets, supported by a board and an advisory group. The archives serve academic researchers, startups and the teams that build language models.
labs.mission: Common Crawl aims to keep a large, current copy of the public web freely available so that anyone can analyze it. It treats open access to crawl data as a way to widen who can do research on the web and on language technology.

about: CompVis is the Computer Vision and Learning group at LMU Munich, formerly the Computer Vision Group at Heidelberg University, led by Prof. Dr. Bjorn Ommer. Its research covers generative visual synthesis, invertible deep models for explainable AI, deep metric and representation learning, and self-supervised learning.

The group is best known for latent diffusion models, presented at CVPR 2022 as a method for high-resolution image synthesis. Source code and models were released on GitHub, and the approach underlies Stable Diffusion.
Newer projects listed on the group's site include SCFlow, TREAD and CleanDIFT. The group also applies its methods to the digital humanities and the life sciences.
labs.mission: The group pursues fundamental research in computer vision and machine learning, with an emphasis on generative models and interpretable representations. It publishes code and models so that others can build on the work.

about: Contextual AI is a company founded in 2023 by Douwe Kiela and Amanpreet Singh, both formerly at Facebook AI Research and Hugging Face. It builds retrieval-augmented generation systems for enterprise use and pairs its commercial platform with research that publishes open code and models.

The company raised a $20 million seed round led by Bain Capital Ventures in June 2023 and an $80 million Series A led by Greycroft in August 2024. Its research includes KTO, an alignment method that needs only a binary signal of whether an output is desirable, and GRIT, which trains one model for both generation and embedding.

Its GitHub and Hugging Face organizations host alignment libraries, retrieval models and an instruction-following reranker released in March 2025, aimed at practitioners who build their own RAG pipelines.
labs.mission: The company works to make language models reliable on enterprise data by grounding them in retrieval. Its open releases are meant to share the underlying alignment and retrieval methods with the research community.

about: Danish Foundation Models is a collaborative effort across Danish universities and research institutions to develop, evaluate and adapt open language AI for Danish society. The core partners are the University of Southern Denmark, Aarhus University through its Center for Humanities Computing, the University of Copenhagen and the Alexandra Institute.

Its members include professors Bolette Sandford Pedersen at Copenhagen, Kristoffer Nielbo at Aarhus and Peter Schneider-Kamp at Southern Denmark, with Kenneth Enevoldsen and many postdoctoral and PhD researchers. The project argues that smaller languages risk exclusion as language models become infrastructure, and it publishes models and datasets openly on Hugging Face.

The 2023 paper Danish Foundation Models set out the program. Danish Dynaword, released in 2025, is an openly licensed, continuously updated collection of Danish text derived from the public parts of the Danish Gigaword, with a companion post-training dataset, dfm-dyna-instruct.
labs.mission: The consortium aims to give Danish society open, well-evaluated language technology that it can adopt and adapt. It treats openness of models and data as a condition for public benefit.

about: Deep Cogito was founded in San Francisco in 2024 by Drishan Arora, who led language-model work for generative search at Google, and Dhruv Malhotra, a former product lead at Google DeepMind. It describes its goal as building general superintelligence and argues that this requires advances in reasoning and iterative self-improvement.

The lab introduced iterated distillation and amplification (IDA) with the Cogito v1 Preview models in April 2025, followed by Cogito v2 Preview in July 2025. Cogito v2.1, released in November 2025 as a 671 billion parameter open-weight model, was post-trained from an openly licensed DeepSeek base model.

In August 2026 the company announced a $43 million Series A led by TQ Ventures, for total funding above $56 million. Reports say the money will fund hiring, training infrastructure, future open-weight Cogito models and an enterprise business.
labs.mission: Deep Cogito pursues models that improve through repeated cycles of search and distillation. It releases open weights as part of that research program.

about: Deep Learning Indaba was conceived to make Africans active shapers and owners of advances in artificial intelligence. The first Indaba ran from 10 to 15 September 2017 at the University of the Witwatersrand in Johannesburg with about 330 delegates, organized by a group that included Shakir Mohamed, Nyalleng Moorosi, Benjamin Rosman, Ulrich Paquet and Vukosi Marivate.

The organization is led by Indaba Abantu, a steering group of Africans across the continent and abroad, with an advisory board and a board of trustees. Its legal entity is Deep Learning Indaba Ltd, a non-profit company limited by guarantee registered in England and Wales. Mohamed, a DeepMind research director, is listed as co-founder and chair of the trustees.

Programs include the annual Indaba, locally organized IndabaX events, a mentorship program and awards. After Johannesburg in 2017 the gathering moved to Stellenbosch in 2018, and it later took place in Accra in 2023. The 2026 edition is planned for Nigeria, and the GitHub organization publishes open practical notebooks from each Indaba.
labs.mission: The Indaba aims to strengthen machine learning and artificial intelligence in Africa and to raise African participation and diversity in the field.

about: DeepSeek was founded on 17 July 2023 as a spin-off from the AI research lab of High-Flyer, a Chinese hedge fund that owns and backs it. Liang Wenfeng founded the company and serves as CEO, and it had about 160 employees in 2025.

The lab released DeepSeek-V2 in May 2024, which introduced multi-head latent attention within a mixture-of-experts design, and DeepSeek-V3 in December 2024. DeepSeek-R1 followed on 20 January 2025 alongside a chatbot, with weights under the MIT License. Later releases include V3.1 in August 2025, V3.2 in December 2025 and a V4 preview in April 2026.

Wikipedia reports that DeepSeek closed a $7 billion Series A at a $52 billion post-money valuation in May 2026, ending its reliance on its parent alone. The company publishes weights and technical reports but not training data, and several governments have restricted its use on official systems.
labs.mission: DeepSeek pursues capable general models and publishes weights and technical reports for them, funded originally by High-Flyer and, from 2026, by outside investors as well.

about: The German Research Center for Artificial Intelligence was established in 1988 as a non-profit public-private partnership. It began in Kaiserslautern and Saarbrücken, and Wolfgang Wahlster has served as its scientific director since the founding.

Today DFKI operates research facilities in Kaiserslautern, Saarbrücken, Bremen, Oldenburg and Osnabrück, laboratories in Berlin, Darmstadt and Lübeck, and a branch office in Trier. Its work is organized into 29 research departments, thirteen competence centers and eight living labs, and it is funded by the European Union, federal ministries, the German states and the German Research Foundation.

DFKI led the national Verbmobil project on speech translation, which produced several spin-off companies and earned the 2001 German Future Prize. Its public code and datasets appear on GitHub and Hugging Face, where researchers in several departments publish benchmarks and models.

DictaLM 2.0 followed in 2024 with an enlarged Hebrew vocabulary, and the DictaLM 3.0 report of February 2026 presents open 24B, 12B and 1.7B models adapted from Mistral Small 3.1, NVIDIA Nemotron Nano V2 and Qwen3, hosted under Apache 2.0.

labs.tagline: The DTAI group at KU Leuven combines machine learning, logic and data mining and is the home of the RobBERT Dutch language models.
about: DTAI is the Declarative Languages and Artificial Intelligence research group in the Department of Computer Science at KU Leuven in Belgium. Its academic staff includes Hendrik Blockeel, Jesse Davis, Luc De Raedt, Tias Guns and Tom Schrijvers, and it is linked to the ADVISE, EAVISE and M-Group research groups.

In January 2020 researchers Pieter Delobelle, Thomas Winters and Bettina Berendt introduced RobBERT, a Dutch RoBERTa-based language model. The group has since refreshed it with RobBERT-2022 and RobBERT-2023, which are published under the DTAI-KULeuven organization on Hugging Face under the MIT license.
labs.mission: To advance machine learning and reasoning methods and to supply open language resources for Dutch.
known_for: Machine learning combined with logic and constraints

labs.name: EdinburghNLP
labs.summary: Natural language processing group at the University of Edinburgh, behind open tools and datasets including the Nematus NMT toolkit and the XSum summarisation dataset.
labs.tagline: EdinburghNLP is the University of Edinburgh's natural language processing group, ranked among the most productive in the world and the home of Nematus.
about: EdinburghNLP brings together faculty, postdocs and PhD students in the School of Informatics. Its research covers language modelling, morphology, parsing, semantics, discourse, generation and machine translation, with links to speech, vision and robotics.

The group reports a faculty of more than a dozen core members and five European Research Council grants, and it is ranked first for NLP output by csrankings.org. It publishes code and data openly, including the Nematus neural machine translation toolkit, the XSum summarization dataset and a widely used list of hallucination-detection papers.
labs.mission: To develop algorithms that let computers understand and produce human language, and to share the resulting tools with the research community.

labs.name: EleutherAI
labs.summary: EleutherAI is a non-profit research institute that trains and releases open models, datasets and tools. It began in 2020 as a Discord server and incorporated in 2023.
labs.tagline: EleutherAI is a non-profit research institute that grew from a Discord server into a leading source of open language models, datasets and evaluation tools.
about: EleutherAI began in July 2020 as a Discord server under the working name LibreAI. Connor Leahy, Leo Gao and Sid Black are named as founders, and the group was renamed EleutherAI later that month. In early 2023 it was incorporated as a non-profit research institute.

It first used compute from Google's TPU Research Cloud and later from CoreWeave. The group released The Pile in December 2020, followed by the GPT-Neo, GPT-J and GPT-NeoX-20B models, and the Pythia suite for studying training dynamics.

Today it reports about fifteen full- and part-time staff along with regular volunteers. Its lm-evaluation-harness, the most starred repository in its GitHub organization, is used widely to benchmark language models.
labs.mission: To advance interpretability and alignment research on open foundation models, keep such models open to study beyond a few companies, and educate the public about their capabilities and risks.

labs.name: ellamind
labs.summary: German company working on AI evaluation, data and agents. It open-sources tooling for evaluation and inference and publishes models and datasets.
labs.tagline: A German AI company, based in Bremen and Berlin, that builds evaluation tools and open-source infrastructure for language models.
about: ellamind GmbH works on evaluation, data and environments for AI systems and helps regulated industries such as health insurance, banking and public administration bring them into production. Its products include elluminate, an agentic evaluation platform, and an accessibility testing agent.

The company open-sources base-eval, curated lm-evaluation-harness task configurations for English and German base models, and inference-hive, distributed LLM inference for SLURM clusters, both under Apache-2.0. It also publishes propella-1, a family of small multilingual annotation models, and sui-1, a 24B-parameter summarization model with inline citations, on Hugging Face.
labs.mission: ellamind focuses on making AI systems measurable and dependable for organisations in regulated sectors, and shares part of its tooling as open source.

labs.name: ELLIS Alicante
labs.summary: ELLIS Alicante is a non-profit research unit of the ELLIS network focused on human-centric AI, with research code and benchmarks on GitHub.
labs.tagline: ELLIS Alicante is a non-profit unit of the European ELLIS network focused on ethical, human-centric AI, directed by Nuria Oliver.
about: ELLIS Alicante was founded in 2020 as a foundation hosting a research unit of the ELLIS network in Spain. It resulted from a 2019 bid, led by Nuria Oliver, for Alicante to host an ELLIS unit, and she serves as its director.

Its research addresses modeling human behavior at individual and societal scales, systems that interact naturally with people, and ethical AI covering fairness, privacy and transparency. It is funded by the Generalitat Valenciana, the European Regional Development Fund and partners including Intel and Fundación Banco Sabadell, and reports over 38 million euros in EU project budgets.

Paper code and evaluation repositories are published on GitHub, including tutorials on graph rewiring and fairness, an open framework for social media AR filters, and evaluations of how language models handle mental-health crises.
labs.mission: To advance ethical, responsible and human-centric artificial intelligence that serves society.
known_for: Open benchmarks on fairness and LLM safety

labs.tagline: The EPFL LLM team built Meditron, an open suite of medical language models, and the Megatron-LLM trainer used to produce them.
about: The EPFL LLM team is a group at the Swiss federal institute in Lausanne that publishes under the epfLLM GitHub and epfl-llm Hugging Face organizations. Its Megatron-LLM repository, created in July 2023, adapts NVIDIA's Megatron-LM trainer for distributed training of open models.

In November 2023 the team released MEDITRON, 7B and 70B-parameter medical models built on Llama-2 and further pretrained on PubMed papers, abstracts and international medical guidelines. The paper reports that MEDITRON-70B outperforms GPT-3.5 and Med-PaLM on four benchmarks, and the team released both model weights and the corpus-building code.
labs.mission: To provide openly available medical language models and training tools so that clinical AI can be studied and improved in the open.

labs.tagline: A research organization that publishes open datasets and analysis on AI compute, hardware, investment and data centers.
about: Epoch AI began in 2021 as a group of volunteers and became a formal organization after its 2022 paper on training compute trends. It describes its aim as helping people understand AI from a neutral perspective grounded in the best available evidence.

Its public databases cover ML hardware, training compute estimates for AI models, AI investment and companies, GPU clusters and AI data centers. It also publishes analysis, chip sales data and polling on AI usage.
labs.mission: Epoch AI seeks to improve society's understanding of the drivers, progress and impact of AI, using data to inform decisions about the technology.

labs.summary: EuroLLM is a series of open multilingual language models for European languages, developed by a consortium of European research institutions and companies under the UTTER project.
labs.tagline: A series of open multilingual language models covering the 24 official EU languages, built by a European research and industry consortium.
about: EuroLLM is developed under the Horizon Europe UTTER project by a consortium that includes Instituto Superior Tecnico, the University of Edinburgh, Instituto de Telecomunicacoes, Universite Paris-Saclay, Unbabel, Sorbonne University, Naver Labs and the University of Amsterdam. The project is funded by Horizon Europe, the European Research Council and EuroHPC.

The models support all 24 official EU languages and training data covers 35 languages. Released models include EuroLLM-1.7B for edge devices, EuroLLM-9B and EuroLLM-22B with a 32K context, in base and instruct versions, available on Hugging Face.
labs.mission: EuroLLM aims to provide fully open language models that serve Europe's linguistic diversity, rather than relying on models centered on English.

labs.mission: FAR.AI aims to close the gap between safety research and real-world adoption so that advanced AI is trustworthy, secure and beneficial.

about: fast.ai was founded in October 2016 by Jeremy Howard and Rachel Thomas with the goal of democratizing deep learning. Sylvain Gugger is also listed as a key person.

Its free course Practical Deep Learning for Coders was first taught at the University of San Francisco and is delivered online with Python as the only prerequisite. In 2018 fast.ai students won Stanford's DAWNBench CIFAR-10 challenge for fastest and cheapest training.
labs.mission: fast.ai works to make deep learning accessible to people from varied backgrounds, through free courses and open-source software.

Bordeaux and is headed by Pierre-Yves Oudeyer, a research director known for work on artificial curiosity and intrinsic motivation.

labs.tagline: A small non-profit Persian NLP lab that published ParsBERT, the first widely used monolingual BERT for Persian, along with Persian GPT-2 and NER models.
about: Hooshvare Research Lab is a Tehran-based group that publishes open models and datasets for Persian natural language processing. Its GitHub organization describes it as a platform for sharing information about artificial intelligence concepts with enthusiasts. The lab's work is published through the Hooshvare organizations on GitHub and Hugging Face.

Its best-known release is ParsBERT, a monolingual BERT-style model for Persian described in a May 2020 preprint by Mehrdad Farahani, Mohammad Gharachorloo, Marzieh Farahani and Mohammad Manthouri. The paper reports gains over multilingual BERT on sentiment analysis, text classification and named entity recognition. The lab later added a Persian GPT-2 model, NER models, a news summarization dataset and workshop materials.
Code and weights are released under permissive licenses such as MIT and Apache 2.0, which has made the models a common baseline for Persian-language research and applications.
labs.mission: The lab aims to make capable language models and datasets for Persian freely available, so that researchers and developers working in the language are not limited to multilingual models built for other languages.

labs.summary: Company behind Colossal-AI distributed training tooling and the Open-Sora video generation models.
labs.tagline: Singapore company behind Colossal-AI, an open-source stack for large-model training, and the Open-Sora video generation models.
about: HPC-AI Tech was founded by Yang You, a professor at the National University of Singapore who earned his PhD at UC Berkeley. The company grew out of research on efficient distributed training and became known for Colossal-AI, an open-source software stack for training and serving large models. It raised a seed round of about six million dollars in 2022 and a 50 million dollar Series A announced in 2024.

Its open-source output includes Colossal-AI and Open-Sora, a video generation project that attracted wide attention on GitHub. Alongside these, the company operates a commercial GPU cloud platform and a model platform with OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic-compatible APIs, and offers enterprise services such as fine-tuning and performance optimization.
The business model combines free open-source infrastructure with paid cloud and services, so the open projects serve as the technical base of the commercial offering.
labs.mission: The company aims to lower the cost and complexity of training and running large AI models, and to keep the core tooling open while selling cloud and enterprise services on top.

labs.name: Hugging Face
labs.summary: The company behind the Hugging Face Hub and open-source libraries such as Transformers, Diffusers and Datasets. Headquartered in New York with a large Paris presence, it hosts the main community platform for open models and datasets.
labs.tagline: The company behind the Hugging Face Hub and the Transformers, Diffusers and Datasets libraries, the central platform for sharing open models and datasets.
about: Hugging Face was founded in 2016 in New York by Clément Delangue, Julien Chaumond and Thomas Wolf. It began as a chatbot app for teenagers and shifted to machine learning tooling after the team open-sourced the model behind the app. Delangue is chief executive, Chaumond is chief technology officer and Wolf is chief science officer.

The company's open-source libraries, notably Transformers, became standard tools for working with pretrained models, and the Hub grew into the main place where researchers and companies publish models and datasets. In 2021 it launched the BigScience workshop, which produced the 176-billion-parameter multilingual BLOOM model in 2022. It also has a large presence in Paris and has expanded into robotics through the 2025 acquisition of Pollen Robotics.

Hugging Face earns revenue from hosted services and enterprise offerings while keeping its libraries and much of its research open. In September 2026 Nvidia announced an agreement to acquire the company, pending regulatory approval.
labs.mission: Hugging Face states its aim as democratizing good machine learning by making models, datasets and tools open and shared by a community.
labs.notice: In September 2026 Nvidia announced a definitive agreement to acquire Hugging Face. The transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2027, and Nvidia has said the platform will remain open and keep operating under the Hugging Face brand.

labs.name: Idiap Research Institute
labs.summary: Independent Swiss non-profit research institute in speech, vision and machine learning that publishes extensive open-source code.
labs.tagline: Independent Swiss non-profit research institute in Martigny working on speech, vision and machine learning, and the home of the original Torch library.
about: Idiap Research Institute was created in 1991 as an autonomous non-profit foundation in Martigny, Switzerland, at the initiative of the Dalle Molle Foundation. Its founding partners include the City of Martigny, the Canton of Valais, EPFL, the University of Geneva and Swisscom. The Swiss Confederation recognizes it as an institute of national importance.

The institute researches speech and audio processing, computer vision, biometrics and machine learning under the tagline Artificial Intelligence for Society. In 2002 researchers there developed Torch, an early machine learning library that is a forerunner of PyTorch. Idiap also coordinated the national research center on interactive multimodal information management from 2001 to 2013, spun out companies such as Klewel in 2007, and has become a certified biometric testing center.
The institute publishes a large amount of open-source code and datasets on GitHub and Hugging Face. As of 2026 it is led by an interim management team while it recruits a new director.
labs.mission: Idiap aims to advance research, innovation and education in artificial intelligence for the benefit of society, while remaining a non-profit and independent institute.

about: The Institute for Language and Speech Processing (ILSP) is part of Athena Research Center in Athens and works on language and speech technology. It has recently marked 35 years of activity. Its research covers language resources, speech processing and, more recently, large language models for Greek.

In March 2024 the institute released Meltemi 7B, trained on a corpus of about 40 billion Greek tokens, and described as the first open large language model for Greek in a July 2024 paper. It followed with Llama-Krikri-8B, built on Llama 3.1 with an extended Greek tokenizer and a 128k context window, trained on about 56.7 billion Greek tokens and supporting polytonic and Ancient Greek.
Models and instruction-tuned variants are published on Hugging Face under the ilsp organization, giving Greek developers and researchers open alternatives to general multilingual models.
labs.mission: ILSP develops language and speech technology for Greek and openly releases the resulting models and resources so that the language is well supported in modern AI systems.

Its open model line includes BgGPT for Bulgarian and MamayLM for Ukrainian, which was developed with ETH Zurich on Gemma 2 9B. In 2024 it also released COMPL-AI, a framework for evaluating models against the EU AI Act.

about: The Institute for Machine Learning at Johannes Kepler University Linz has been led since 2018 by Sepp Hochreiter. Hochreiter developed the long short-term memory architecture in his 1991 diploma thesis and published it with Jürgen Schmidhuber in 1997. He previously led the university's Institute of Bioinformatics and heads the LIT AI Lab, which he took over in 2017.

The group works on machine learning and statistical methods. Its researchers introduced modern Hopfield networks with continuous states in 2020 and applied them to immune repertoire classification. In 2024 the group and collaborators published xLSTM, an extended LSTM architecture presented at NeurIPS, and the company NXAI, where Hochreiter is chief scientist, builds industrial models on it.
Code and models appear on the institute's GitHub and Hugging Face organizations.
labs.mission: The institute develops and applies machine learning and statistical methods, with a stated emphasis on deep learning fundamentals and their use in science and industry.

labs.name: Institute of Foundation Models
labs.summary: Research institute at MBZUAI in Abu Dhabi that sponsors LLM360, the open model and data effort. The legacy LLM360 Hugging Face organization notes that its namespace has moved to the Institute of Foundation Models.
labs.tagline: MBZUAI research institute that sponsors LLM360, the fully open effort behind the Amber, K2 and TxT360 releases, and the K2 Horizon model family.
about: The Institute of Foundation Models (IFM) is a research unit of the Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence in Abu Dhabi, launched publicly in May 2025. The LLM360 project, which states it is proudly sponsored by the institute, publishes open large language models together with their training data, code and checkpoints. The LLM360 Hugging Face organization notes that its namespace has moved to IFM.

LLM360's releases include Amber-7B, Crystal-7B, the 65-billion-parameter K2 trained on 1.4 trillion tokens, and TxT360, a pre-training dataset that deduplicates 99 Common Crawl snapshots and 14 other sources. In September 2026 the institute released K2 Horizon, six fully open models from 0.9 to 375 billion parameters.
The institute also coordinates the Jais Arabic models and operates with a Silicon Valley lab alongside its Abu Dhabi base.
labs.mission: LLM360 aims to enable community-owned AI through open large model research, creating standards and tools for capability and knowledge transfer. The institute releases weights, code, data and training details.

about: The Institute of Smart Systems and Artificial Intelligence (ISSAI) was founded in September 2019 at Nazarbayev University in Astana. It was set up to build national research capacity in artificial intelligence and draws on experience from institutions in Asia, Europe and North America. Its home is the university's campus on Kabanbay Batyr Avenue.

ISSAI is known for open resources for the Kazakh language, including the Kazakh Speech Corpus, whose second edition holds about 1,200 hours of transcribed speech with Kazakh-Russian code-switching, and the KazakhTTS corpora. It worked with the Ministry of Science and Higher Education on KazLLM, whose open-source version is on Hugging Face.
The institute also runs applied projects such as the Tilsync partnership offering and publishes code on GitHub under the IS2AI organization.
labs.mission: ISSAI aims to develop a national capacity for artificial intelligence research in Kazakhstan, with a focus on the Kazakh language and open resources.

labs.summary: Data-science lab within the National Library of Sweden that builds language and speech models from the library's collections. Its models are openly available on Hugging Face.
labs.tagline: Data lab inside the National Library of Sweden that trains open Swedish language and speech models, including KB-BERT and KB-Whisper, on the library's collections.
about: KBLab is a research department within the National Library of Sweden, set up in 2019 as a national research infrastructure for digital humanities and social science. It gives researchers access to the library's collections in structured form. The lab is directed by Love Börjeson.

Using the legal-deposit and digitized holdings, KBLab trains Swedish models. Its 2020 paper by Martin Malmsten, Love Börjeson and Chris Haffenden introduced KB-BERT. The lab later released KB-Whisper, speech recognition models trained on more than 50,000 hours of Swedish speech, which it reports outperform OpenAI's Whisper at each size on Swedish.
Models are published on Hugging Face, with the large KB-Whisper model under the Apache 2.0 license.
labs.mission: KBLab aims to make the National Library's collections usable for research through language and speech models and open tools, supporting digital humanities and social science.

about: The Kempelen Institute of Intelligent Technologies (KInIT) is an independent, non-profit institute in Bratislava. It was set up with backing from Slovak companies including ESET, Tatra banka, Innovatrics and Softec, and aims to connect the private and public sectors with multidisciplinary research. Mária Bieliková is Director General.

Its research areas include web and user data processing and disinformation, natural language processing, data analysis for green energy, information security, and ethics of intelligent technologies. In 2021 its NLP team consulted on and evaluated SlovakBERT, the first public large neural language model for Slovak, trained with partner Gerulata Technologies.
The institute publishes Slovak models and benchmarks, including the 2025 skLEP benchmark, on Hugging Face and GitHub.

about: Kotoba Technologies was founded in 2023 by Noriyuki Kojima, chief executive, and Jungo Kasai, chief technology officer. The company is incorporated in San Francisco with a Tokyo operations office and describes itself as a frontier voice AI company with expertise in East Asian languages.

labs.name: Kyutai
labs.summary: Paris-based open-science AI lab focused on speech and multimodal models. It publishes weights, code and papers for its work.
labs.tagline: Paris non-profit open-science lab building speech-native and multimodal models, creator of Moshi, Mimi, Unmute and Helium.
about: Kyutai is an open-science AI research lab in Paris, funded by the Iliad Group, the CMA CGM Group and Schmidt Sciences. Its team is led by Patrick Pérez as chief executive, with Alexandre Défossez as head of research and Laurent Mazaré as head of engineering. Edouard Grave and Hervé Jegou are listed among its alumni.

The lab is known for Moshi, described as the first speech-native dialogue system, which processes speech directly rather than converting it to text and back. It also released Unmute, which gives any text model real-time listening and speaking, and Helium, a multilingual two-billion-parameter language model. Papers, code and weights are published openly.
Its recent research output covers text-to-speech, video autoencoders and world models.
labs.mission: Kyutai aims to advance open research on speech and multimodal AI, publishing models, code and papers for the community.

labs.name: LAION
labs.summary: LAION is a non-profit making datasets, tools and models openly available for research. It also co-organised the OpenAssistant crowd-sourced conversation project.
labs.tagline: German non-profit that releases large open datasets, tools and models for AI research, best known for LAION-400M, LAION-5B and OpenCLIP.
about: LAION, the Large-scale Artificial Intelligence Open Network, is a non-profit research network based in Germany that makes machine learning resources available to the public. It is supported by donations and public research grants. Its volunteers include Christoph Schuhmann, Jenia Jitsev and Romain Beaumont.

In 2021 it released LAION-400M, an image-text dataset recreating the kind of data used for CLIP, followed by LAION-5B in 2022, the largest openly available image-text dataset at the time. Stable Diffusion was trained on it, and LAION members helped train OpenCLIP models on it. In 2023 it co-organised the OpenAssistant crowd-sourced conversation project.
After Stanford researchers reported suspected abuse material links in LAION-5B in December 2023, LAION withdrew its datasets and in August 2024 released a cleaned Re-LAION-5B.
labs.mission: LAION states that it makes large-scale machine learning resources, including datasets, tools and open models, available to the public for research and education.

about: lang-uk is an informal community of programmers, linguists and researchers that supports existing projects and starts new ones to collect Ukrainian text corpora and other language data. Its work is hosted in the lang-uk GitHub organization and on Hugging Face, and the community is open to new members. Ukrainian media first covered its results after its first year of work in 2015.

Co-founder Vsevolod Dyomkin has described the project's main task as collecting and maintaining data, models and tools for processing Ukrainian. Mariana Romanyshyn led a group of linguists who began collecting open Ukrainian text data, and Dmytro Chaplynskyi is credited on the UberText 2.0 corpus paper. The Ukrainian Catholic University and the Kyiv School of Economics are listed as partners.
Its resources serve scientists, entrepreneurs and journalists, covering services, models, libraries, dictionaries, gazetteers, corpora and datasets.
labs.mission: The community aims to create the conditions for full processing of Ukrainian-language text by gathering and openly sharing corpora, tools and models.

about: The Language Technology Group (LTG) is part of the Department of Informatics at the University of Oslo, led by Lilja Øvrelid. Its members include Stephan Oepen, Erik Velldal, Andrey Kutuzov, Yves Scherrer, Pierre Lison and David Samuel. The group works on natural language processing and large language models, including for Norwegian.

It released NorBERT in January 2021 and NorBERT 2 in February 2022, then the NorBERT 3 family and the NorBench benchmark in 2023. The group has also trained generative Norwegian models such as NorMistral and NorBLOOM. Projects it participates in include HPLT, OpenEuroLLM, NorwAI, Integreat and MediaFutures.
The group coordinates the Nordic Language Processing Laboratory and publishes code and models on GitHub and Hugging Face.
labs.mission: LTG develops language technology and language models, with a focus on Norwegian and openly available resources for evaluation and training.

labs.name: Latam-GPT
labs.summary: Latam-GPT is a Latin American language model project coordinated by CENIA, Chile's national AI centre. It publishes models, a regional text corpus, benchmarks and data-curation tools openly.
labs.tagline: Latin American open language model project coordinated by Chile's national AI centre CENIA, released in 2026 with a regional text corpus.
about: Latam-GPT is a regional initiative to build a language model entirely within Latin America, for Latin America. It is coordinated by CENIA, the Chilean national AI centre, whose director Álvaro Soto spoke for the project at its launch. Reports describe a network of more than thirty institutions across the region.

Chile launched the model on 10 February 2026 as open infrastructure for developers, trained on more than eight terabytes of Latin American data in Spanish and Portuguese, with indigenous languages planned. Press reports give its cost as about 550,000 dollars, funded by CAF and CENIA, with a first version trained on cloud infrastructure and later versions planned for a supercomputer at the University of Tarapacá.
Models, data and tools are published on GitHub and Hugging Face, and the model is free for companies and public institutions to build on.
labs.mission: The project aims to give the region a model that represents its languages, culture and context, and to let developers build region-specific applications without depending on models made elsewhere.

labs.summary: Lelapa AI is a South African startup building language AI for African languages, including a commercial speech and translation product called Vulavula. It also releases research models and datasets openly, notably InkubaLM.

about: Lelapa AI was founded in Johannesburg in 2022 by Pelonomi Moiloa, Jade Abbott and academic collaborators, and the name means home in Sotho and Tswana. Moiloa is chief executive and Abbott is chief technology officer, and the team page also lists Vukosi Marivate as chief information officer, Benjamin Rosman as chief scientist and George Konidaris as an advisor. Brown University and Wired have described Moiloa, Abbott, Marivate, Konidaris, Rosman and Pravesh Ranchod as the founding group.

The company's commercial product line is Vulavula, with Vulavula Transcribe for multilingual contact centres and Vulavula Translate for translation between African languages. It targets telecoms and financial services.
Lelapa also releases research models and datasets openly, notably InkubaLM, and states that it builds resource-efficient language AI designed to scale.
labs.mission: Lelapa states that it builds resource-efficient language AI for global scale, starting with African languages that are poorly served by existing models.

labs.mission: LLM-jp aims to build open Japanese large language models, share knowledge among researchers and enable cross-organization collaboration on data and compute.

labs.tagline: Open lab begun at Stanford that develops foundation models in public, releasing code, data, weights and experiment logs for Marin 8B and 32B.
about: Marin is an open lab started in 2024 at Stanford University by David Hall and Percy Liang. It is primarily developed by Open Athena with community contributors, and it releases its discussions, code, model weights, data sources, successful and failed experiments and tools for learning.

The lab released an 8B model in May 2025 and a 32B model in October 2025. Google's open source team reported that Marin 32B beat Olmo 2 32B on 32 of 42 tasks, and the model is released under Apache 2.0. Later work covers mixture-of-experts training, a scaling suite called Delphi, a 25-trillion-token data pipeline and post-training data.
Everything is documented in public pages so others can reproduce and extend runs.
labs.mission: Marin aims to develop foundation models in the open, sharing every step from data to weights so the community can learn from and build on them.

about: The Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence was initiated in October 2019 and licensed by the UAE Ministry of Education in April 2020. Sir J. Its graduate programs launched in January 2021 and the first MSc cohort graduated in January 2023. By 2025 it had 84 faculty and more than 200 postdocs and researchers.

The Institute of Foundation Models, launched in May 2025, coordinates the Jais Arabic models and the K2 family. In September 2026 it released K2 Horizon, six open models from 0.9B to 375B parameters, with weights, code, data and methodology.

about: Mesolitica was founded in Kuala Lumpur by Khalil Nooh, chief executive, and Husein Zolkepli, chief technology officer. The team traces the work behind MaLLaM to January 2019, and its GitHub organization dates from February 2019.

It launched MaLLaM, a Malaysian language model trained on nearly 200 billion tokens of Malay content, in December 2023. In January 2024 it published papers on MaLLaM and on Malaysian Mistral, a Mistral 7B model finetuned on Malaysian data, and released models on Hugging Face. It also works on speech systems and voice agents.
The company says it runs operations within Malaysia and open-sources its datasets on GitHub while allowing owners to request removal of their content.
labs.mission: Mesolitica aims to bring AI to Bahasa Melayu speakers and promote AI sovereignty by working entirely within Malaysia.

labs.name: METR
labs.summary: Nonprofit that evaluates frontier AI models for autonomous capabilities and publishes evaluation code and datasets.
labs.tagline: A Berkeley nonprofit that measures what frontier AI agents can do on long, autonomous tasks and publishes the evidence for governments, labs and the public.
about: METR, short for Model Evaluation and Threat Research, is a nonprofit based in Berkeley, California. It began as ARC Evals, the evaluation arm of the Alignment Research Center, and was spun out as an independent organization in December 2023 under founder and CEO Beth Barnes.

The group builds task suites and measurement methods for autonomous AI agents, and publishes the results. Its best-known metric, the task-completion time horizon, expresses how long a task, measured by human expert completion time, an agent can finish at a given success rate. It also runs applied assessments with AI developers, including pre-deployment evaluations and incident investigations.

METR states that it is funded by donations and has not accepted funding from AI companies, although developers provide access and tokens for evaluations. It has worked with several frontier developers and provides technical assistance to the European AI Office.
labs.mission: METR aims to discover and publish evidence on the capabilities of advanced AI systems, the risks they pose and the effectiveness of mitigations, so that the world can avoid catastrophic mistakes.

about: Mila, the Quebec AI Institute, traces its origin to the lab Yoshua Bengio founded at the Université de Montréal in 1993. In 2017 it grew into a collaboration between the Université de Montréal and McGill University with Polytechnique Montréal and HEC Montréal, and it became a non-profit in 2018.

The institute brings together academic researchers and students working on deep learning, reinforcement learning, health, climate, responsible AI and related areas. It reports a community of more than 1,400 people and runs training programs, an AI policy fellowship and a venture program alongside research.
Mila lists 34 open-source projects, including Theano, an early deep learning framework that originated there, SpeechBrain, TorchDrug, BabyAI and Orion.
labs.mission: Mila aims to be a global hub for scientific advances that drive AI innovation for everyone's benefit, built on collaboration, excellence and ethics.

about: MiniMax was founded in December 2021 in Shanghai by Yan Junjie, Yun Yeyi and Zhou Yucong, who came from computer vision research at SenseTime. It began research in January 2022 and released its first text model, abab1, in April 2022. The company listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in January 2026.

The MiniMax-M series of language models is published on Hugging Face under the MiniMaxAI organization, with recent releases including MiniMax-M3, M3.1-Flash and the H3 image models. MiniMax is a commercial, publicly listed company that releases some weights openly.

labs.name: Mistral AI
labs.summary: Paris-based company building frontier language, vision and speech models. It publishes many of its models as open weights alongside a commercial API.
labs.tagline: A Paris AI company that pairs open-weight models under permissive licenses with a commercial platform, positioning itself as Europe's frontier lab.
about: Mistral AI was founded in April 2023 in Paris by Arthur Mensch, Guillaume Lample and Timothée Lacroix, who had met at École polytechnique and worked at Google DeepMind and Meta. Its first model, Mistral 7B, was released on 27 September 2023 under the Apache 2.0 license.

The company builds language, coding, speech, document and forecasting models, and sells them through its Studio and Vibe products and through sovereign deployments for enterprises and governments. Recent open-weight releases include Mistral Small 4 under Apache 2.0, Voxtral TTS and the one-trillion-parameter Mistral Large 4.
Mistral is venture-funded and commercial. ASML took an 11 percent shareholding in 2025, and the firm is often cited as a leading beneficiary of European digital sovereignty policy.
labs.mission: Mistral says its goal is to put frontier AI in everyone's hands, keeping it open and giving organizations control and ownership of their AI systems.

about: Mixedbread is an applied research lab focused on retrieval. It builds embedding, reranking and search systems that give AI applications the right context at the right time.

Recent work covers listwise rerankers, quantization for late-interaction retrieval and ingestion of very large files.

about: Miðeind was founded in 2015 by Vilhjálmur Þorsteinsson, a long-time software entrepreneur. It develops language technology and AI for Icelandic, a language whose small market, limited data and complex grammar leave it poorly served by large technology firms.

Its products include Málfríður for spelling and grammar correction, Hreimur for speech recognition, Erlendur for translation, Snara for dictionary search and Lísa for text extraction, all gathered on the Málstaður site. The company states that its software is mostly open source.

Miðeind was an implementation partner in the Icelandic government's Language Technology Programme from 2019 to 2022 and maintains a Hugging Face leaderboard that evaluates large language models on Icelandic.

labs.name: MLCommons
labs.summary: MLCommons is a consortium that publishes the MLPerf benchmarks, open datasets such as People's Speech and the AILuminate safety benchmark. Reference implementations are on GitHub and datasets on Hugging Face.
labs.tagline: A vendor-neutral consortium that builds and publishes the MLPerf benchmarks, open datasets and AI safety measurements used across the industry.
about: MLCommons grew out of MLPerf, a benchmarking effort begun in 2018 after engineers and researchers from Baidu, Google, Harvard, Stanford and UC Berkeley began meeting to agree on common ways to measure machine learning performance. The MLCommons association was launched in December 2020 to give that work, and related dataset and tooling projects, a permanent home.

Its working groups publish benchmark suites for training, inference, high-performance computing, mobile and tiny devices, together with reference implementations on GitHub. Datasets such as People's Speech and tooling such as MLCube are released openly.

Since 2023 an AI Risk and Reliability group has built safety measurement, which produced the AILuminate benchmark for large language models in December 2024. Member companies, universities and non-profits fund and govern the consortium, and its results are widely cited by hardware vendors and cloud providers.
labs.mission: MLCommons states its mission as standardizing AI measurement so that buyers, builders and policymakers can make informed decisions about accuracy, safety, speed and efficiency.

about: The Maltese Language Resource Server is a University of Malta project that produces tools and resources for Maltese, English and Maltese Sign Language. It is coordinated by the Institute of Linguistics and Language Technology together with the Department of Artificial Intelligence.

The server hosts Korpus Malti, an annotated corpus of roughly 250 million tokens in its version 3.0, as well as a learner corpus, an open lexicon and a sign language dictionary. A 2016 electronic Maltese dictionary built on the group's lexicon was launched with the Malta Communications Authority.
More recently the group has released Maltese language models and datasets on Hugging Face under the MLRS organisation, for researchers and developers working on Maltese.
labs.mission: The project aims to supply the open language data and software that Maltese needs to be supported by modern language technology.

labs.tagline: Compact open-weight vision-language models for detection, captioning and segmentation, now part of Prime Intellect.
about: Moondream is a family of small vision-language models built by M87 Labs. The models handle captioning, querying, detection, pointing and segmentation, and run on GPUs, CPUs and edge hardware.

Moondream 3.1 uses a sparse mixture-of-experts design with 9 billion parameters, 2 billion of them active. The site reports more than five million monthly downloads, open weights and commercial use permitted. The company also offers a hosted API, a fine-tuning product and the Photon inference engine.
In October 2026 Moondream announced that it had been acquired by Prime Intellect, which says the combined team will accelerate open models and fast multimodal AI.
labs.mission: Moondream aims to make capable visual AI small and fast enough to be fine-tuned and deployed on real-world edge cases anywhere.
labs.notice: Moondream announced on 14 October 2026 that it had been acquired by Prime Intellect, another lab in this atlas.

labs.name: Moonshot AI
labs.summary: Beijing company behind the Kimi assistant and model family. It publishes Kimi model weights on Hugging Face.
labs.tagline: Beijing lab behind the Kimi models, whose open-weight Kimi K3 family at 2.8 trillion parameters is the largest open release to date.
about: Moonshot AI was founded in Beijing in March 2023 by Yang Zhilin, Zhou Xinyu and Wu Yuxin, who had been schoolfriends at Tsinghua University. Yang previously worked at Google Brain and Meta. The company is named after Pink Floyd's The Dark Side of the Moon.

It operates the Kimi assistant, an API platform and the Kimi Code command-line agent, and publishes model weights on Hugging Face. Kimi K2 appeared in July 2025, K2.5 added native vision in January 2026, K3 followed in mid-2026 and Kimi K3.1 Pro was published in November 2026.
Moonshot is venture-backed, with Alibaba and Tencent among its investors, and releases K3 under a custom license that requires revenue sharing from very large commercial inference providers.
labs.mission: Moonshot states its aim as building foundation models toward artificial general intelligence, sharing research with the open-source community.

labs.name: Motif Technologies
labs.summary: Korean AI company publishing Motif base models and open optimizer and activation kernels.
labs.tagline: Korean AI lab, a spin-off of the infrastructure firm Moreh, publishing open-weight Motif language models and the training techniques behind them.
about: Motif Technologies is a Korean AI company reported to have been established in February 2025 as a spin-off from the AI infrastructure company Moreh. It trains its own foundation models, led by CEO Junghwan Lim according to press reports and its technical report.

Its Hugging Face organization carries the Motif model family, including the Motif-2-12.7B open-weight model described in a November 2025 technical report, as well as audio, vision encoder, video and VAE components. The report describes a new attention design, a curriculum-based data schedule and optimized training kernels.

Motif-3, a sparse mixture-of-experts model with about 314 billion parameters, was published in August 2026 under a non-commercial research license, a departure from the Apache 2.0 license used for Motif-2. Press reports link its training to South Korea's national sovereign-AI program.
labs.mission: Motif aims to build competitive, domestically developed foundation models and the efficient training methods behind them.

labs.name: Mozilla.ai
labs.summary: Public benefit company founded by Mozilla (a subsidiary of the Mozilla Foundation) building open-source tools for trustworthy, user-controlled AI such as llamafile, any-llm and any-agent.
labs.tagline: Mozilla-backed company building open-source tools that give people and organizations choice, transparency and control over how AI is used.
about: Mozilla.ai is a distributed company backed by the Mozilla Foundation that builds open-source AI products and infrastructure. Its GitHub organization dates from April 2023.

Its tools include any-llm, a single interface to many model providers, any-agent for running and evaluating agent frameworks, any-guardrail, mcpd, encoderfile and the Lumigator evaluation platform. It also hosts llamafile, the project that packages a model as one executable. Its newer products are Otari, an open-source governance layer for AI agents, and Octonous.
The team values open foundations and keeps humans in charge of outcomes; the code is largely released under Apache 2.0.
labs.mission: Mozilla.ai builds open-source AI products and infrastructure that give people and organizations more choice, transparency and control.

labs.summary: Music Technology Group at Universitat Pompeu Fabra, a research group building open-source audio and music analysis software including the Essentia library.
labs.tagline: The Barcelona research group behind Essentia and Freesound-linked work, building open audio and music analysis software since 1994.
about: The Music Technology Group is a research group of the Department of Information and Communication Technologies at Universitat Pompeu Fabra in Barcelona. It was founded in 1994 by Xavier Serra, who still directs it.
Its research covers audio signal processing, sound and music description, musical interaction, and sound and music communities. The group releases much of its software as open source on GitHub.

Its best known software is Essentia, a C++ library with Python bindings for audio analysis and music information retrieval. The library began in 2006 to replace a set of ad hoc C++ programs and is released under the AGPLv3 licence.
labs.mission: The group works to advance sound and music computing and to turn that research into open tools used by scientists, developers and artists.
