labs.summary: AI lab at the National Library of Norway that trains and releases Norwegian language and speech models from the library's digital collections.
labs.tagline: The National Library of Norway's AI lab, which releases Norwegian language models, speech models and datasets built from the library's collections.
about: The AI-lab at the National Library of Norway explores how AI can serve libraries, archives and museums, and builds datasets and models for the wider community. It is a unit of the library rather than a separate company.

Its first major output, the Norwegian Transformer Model Project of 2020 to 2021, produced nb-bert-base, described as the first working Norwegian transformer model, and the Norwegian Colossal Corpus. A later Norwegian Speech Transformer Project, led by Per Egil Kummervold from September 2022, targeted better Norwegian speech-to-text.
The lab publishes its work through its GitHub and Hugging Face organizations.
labs.mission: The lab pursues applications of AI in libraries, archives and museums and contributes datasets and models so that the library can help shape good AI for Norwegian.

It builds ultra-low-latency speech that can run locally, on premises or through an API, with multilingual voices and instant voice cloning. Its site lists the NeuTTS family and the NeuCodec audio codec and links to its GitHub and Hugging Face organizations.
The company has reported more than one million open-source downloads and says it is partnering with device makers.

labs.summary: Open-source interpretability platform for exploring, visualising and steering model internals such as sparse autoencoder features.
labs.tagline: An open-source interpretability platform for exploring, visualizing and steering model internals such as sparse autoencoder features.
about: Neuronpedia was created by Johnny Lin, an engineer who previously worked at Apple. It is an open-source platform where researchers and the public can search the features inside language models, steer model behavior and trace circuits.

It hosts feature dashboards and tooling for releases such as Gemma Scope 2, Llama Scope and SAE Bench, and recent additions include Circuit Tracer, the Assistant Axis, Natural Language Autoencoders and Jacobian Lens. It also offers an API and a community Slack.
Funding comes from Decode Research, Open Philanthropy, the Long Term Future Fund and others, and its users include groups at Anthropic, Google DeepMind, EleutherAI and Apollo Research.
labs.mission: Neuronpedia aims to make model internals easy to inspect and share, so that interpretability research is open and collaborative.

Its Hugging Face organisation PORTULAN hosts the Albertina encoder family in European and Brazilian Portuguese, from 100 million to 1.5 billion parameters, and the Gervasio decoder models at 8 and 70 billion parameters.
The group also publishes benchmark datasets such as extraglue and glue-ptpt and maintains a leaderboard of open language models for Portuguese.

about: Nomic was founded in 2022 in New York. Its early work focused on open research and tools for understanding the data behind AI models, including the Atlas data explorer, GPT4All and the Nomic Embed models, which were released with open weights, open data and training code.

Working with engineering firms led the company to focus on drawings, specifications, codes and project data. Its platform now offers agents and an API for architecture, engineering and construction, along with a benchmark called AEC-Bench.
Coatue led a 17 million dollar Series A in 2023, and Aurecon and Arcadis joined as strategic investors in 2026.
labs.mission: Nomic says AI should give experts more time to be experts, taking on repetitive work while accountable professionals stay in control of results.

labs.summary: Norwegian Research Center for AI Innovation at NTNU, publishing open-weight Norwegian language models.
labs.tagline: NTNU's national AI innovation centre, publishing Norwegian large language models for research and experimentation.
about: NorwAI is the Norwegian Research Center for AI Innovation at NTNU in Trondheim, started in October 2020 and directed by Professor Jon Atle Gulla. It combines academic research with industry partners that apply AI.
In May 2024 the centre launched a suite of Norwegian large language models, built by adapting open architectures such as Mistral and Llama to Norwegian data and trained on NTNU's Idun cluster.

Models are hosted on Hugging Face and can be downloaded free of charge for research and experiments. The centre states it has neither the mandate nor the resources to serve them as a permanent public API.
labs.mission: NorwAI aims to build Norwegian-language AI capacity and to carry research results into Norwegian industry and public services.

Funding includes a 50 million dollar Series A led by Paradigm in April 2025 and a 90 million dollar round announced in October 2026.

about: NovaSky is a team within the Sky Computing Lab at UC Berkeley. Its GitHub organization was created in January 2025, the month it published Sky-T1, a reasoning model it said could be trained for under 450 dollars.

The group releases weights, data and training code together. After Sky-T1 it published work on cutting reasoning costs, test-time scaling for code generation and the SkyRL framework, which grew from SkyRL-v0 for long-horizon software agents into a modular RL library for training LLMs.
Its repositories, including SkyThought and SkyRL, are released under Apache 2.0, and its audience is researchers and developers training reasoning and agentic models.

labs.summary: NVIDIA is a large public company best known for GPUs, and it also publishes a broad set of open models, datasets and training software. Its open releases include the Nemotron language models, Cosmos world models, GR00T robotics models, and the NeMo speech toolkit with Parakeet and Canary models.
labs.tagline: A GPU maker that also releases open models, datasets and tooling, from Nemotron language models to Cosmos world models and speech ASR.
about: NVIDIA was founded in 1993 by Jensen Huang, Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem and is headquartered in Santa Clara, California. It is primarily a hardware and software platform company, and its open-model work sits alongside that business.

Through its Hugging Face organization and GitHub, NVIDIA publishes model checkpoints, large synthetic and curated datasets, and training and inference software. Main families include Nemotron for language and reasoning, Cosmos for physical-AI world models, Isaac GR00T for humanoid robots, and Parakeet, Canary and Magpie for speech.

Research is published as technical reports on arXiv, often with long author lists, and many releases come with training recipes and data. NVIDIA says its Nemotron effort includes open weights, open datasets and published methods.
labs.mission: NVIDIA presents its open releases as a way to let developers and organizations build, customize and deploy AI on its platform, including sovereign and domain-specific systems. It describes Nemotron as open technology covering models, data and recipes.
labs.notice: NVIDIA is a large public company, listed here for its extensive open model and dataset releases. Not all of its products or models are open, and licence terms differ by model.

labs.name: NXAI
labs.summary: Linz-based company commercialising xLSTM research from the JKU Linz group. It publishes xLSTM models, TiRex time-series forecasters and kernels.
labs.tagline: Linz company commercializing Sepp Hochreiter's xLSTM research, publishing xLSTM models, TiRex time-series forecasters and fast recurrent kernels.
about: NXAI was set up in early 2024 in Linz, Austria, by Sepp Hochreiter, who leads the Institute for Machine Learning at JKU Linz, together with the company builder Netural X and PIERER Digital Holding. Hochreiter is Chief Scientist and Albert Ortig is CEO, according to press coverage.

The company aims to turn research on sequence modeling into industrial applications in engineering, robotics, automation and process control. It publishes the xLSTM architecture code, FlashRNN kernels, Vision-LSTM and the TiRex family of zero-shot time-series forecasting models.
Its GitHub organization dates from May 2024, and recent Hugging Face releases include TiRex-2 forecasting assets and KronLSTM language models.
labs.mission: NXAI states that its mission is to turn pioneering research into market-relevant industrial AI by building scalable, generalist foundation models.

about: Occiglot describes itself as an ongoing research collective and an informal community of motivated individuals building open multilingual language models for Europe. Its announcement in March 2024 framed the work as preserving linguistic diversity and AI sovereignty in Europe.

The group released continually pre-trained Occiglot-7B models for German, French, Italian, Spanish and combined European language sets in March 2024, followed by the Occiglot-Fineweb dataset and German models built with DiscoResearch. The page names contributors Manuel Brack, Malte Ostendorff and Pedro Ortiz Suarez, and invites collaborators through its Discord server.

The organization reports reductions in forecasting error and cost savings for grid operators and publishes models and code on GitHub and Hugging Face.

about: OpenBMB, short for Open Lab for Big Model Base, describes its goal as building foundation models and systems toward AGI. It is the open-source community associated with ModelBest, a Beijing company founded in August 2022 as a spin-off from Tsinghua University's Natural Language Processing Laboratory.

ModelBest was founded with Li Dahai as CEO and Liu Zhiyuan as Chief Scientist, according to press and encyclopedic sources. The community's flagship releases are the MiniCPM small language models and the MiniCPM-V multimodal models for local devices, along with VoxCPM for speech and the UltraRAG framework.
ModelBest says the MiniCPM series has passed 24 million downloads, and its models appear in phones and cars.
labs.mission: OpenBMB aims to build foundation models and systems toward AGI, with efficient models that run on consumer devices.

labs.summary: German publicly funded research consortium that trained the Teuken open multilingual language models for European languages.
labs.tagline: German publicly funded consortium that trained the open Teuken-7B models, built from scratch for all 24 official languages of the European Union.
about: OpenGPT-X was a collaborative project funded by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Climate Action from January 2022 to December 2024. It brought together partners from industry, research and media, with Fraunhofer IAIS and IIS leading and compute from the Jülich Supercomputing Centre.

Its main output was Teuken-7B, a seven-billion-parameter model trained from scratch on the 24 official EU languages, with about half of its pretraining data not in English. Instruct and base versions appeared on Hugging Face from September 2024, and the project issued its public press release on 26 November 2024.
The team also published a European LLM Leaderboard in July 2024 and an LLM Workbook, and Deutsche Telekom's T-Systems became the first provider to move Teuken from research to commercial use.
labs.mission: OpenGPT-X set out to develop versatile, trustworthy, multilingual and open language models made in Germany and to support their adoption in the German economy.

labs.summary: French open-source community building open French-language models and datasets. It released the Lucie and Luciole models.
labs.tagline: French community and BPI-funded consortium building open commons for French, including the Lucie-7B and Luciole model families.
about: OpenLLM France grew out of a community of academic and industry stakeholders interested in open-source generative models, with a GitHub organization created in June 2023. Its current research project is funded by BPI France for two years and run by a consortium of nine official partners with 12 associate partners.

about: OpenLLM-Ro is a community building open large language models for Romanian. Its GitHub organization was created in April 2024, and its first Romanian models, fine-tuned from Llama 2, appeared on 14 May 2024.

labs.name: OpenThoughts
labs.summary: Open research collective curating fully open datasets and recipes for reasoning models, led with Bespoke Labs and academic partners; releases OpenThoughts datasets and OpenThinker models.
labs.tagline: A research collective curating fully open reasoning datasets and recipes, from the OpenThoughts3 data recipe to the OpenThinker models.
about: OpenThoughts is a collaboration of researchers and engineers from universities including Stanford, UC Berkeley, UT Austin, NYU, the University of Washington and TUM, together with LAION. It launched publicly in January 2025 with the aim of producing open post-training data for reasoning models.

The project publishes datasets, training code and models together. Its OpenThoughts3 recipe, described in the paper "OpenThoughts: Data Recipes for Reasoning Models", was derived from more than 1,000 controlled experiments and produced the 1.2 million example OpenThoughts3 dataset and the OpenThinker3-7B model.

Compute and support come from academic centers such as the Jülich Supercomputing Centre, TACC and TU Dresden, as well as industry partners. From late 2025 the group extended its work to agentic tasks under the OpenThoughts-Agent project.
labs.mission: OpenThoughts aims to make the data side of reasoning models as open as the weights, so that the community can study which data choices matter. It treats systematic, reproducible ablation of data pipelines as its main method.

about: Oumi emerged from stealth in January 2025 with a $10 million seed round and an open-source platform covering the model lifecycle, from data preparation and training to evaluation and deployment. It was built with researchers from more than a dozen universities.

The company is led by co-founder and CEO Manos Koukoumidis, a former Google Cloud engineering manager, with co-founder Oussama Elachqar and other founders who say they worked on PaLM at Google. Alongside the open library, Oumi offers a commercial platform with an agent that automates evaluation, data curation and training for teams building specialized models.
labs.mission: Oumi wants AI development to be collective and reproducible, with open code, data and models rather than closed stacks. It describes its aim as giving AI a shared, Linux-like open foundation.

about: Physical Intelligence builds general-purpose foundation models for robots rather than robot hardware. The company was co-founded by Karol Hausman, Sergey Levine, Chelsea Finn and others, and draws on research from Google, UC Berkeley and Stanford.

Its pi0 model combines a vision-language backbone with a flow-matching action expert to generate robot actions. The company released pi0 weights and training and inference code through the openpi repository in early 2025.
Researchers and robotics developers use openpi to fine-tune policies on their own robots, which makes the project one of the main open entry points to robot foundation models.
labs.mission: The company aims to build a general-purpose model that can control many kinds of robots across many tasks. It shares part of its research openly to help the field progress.

about: Pluralis Research was founded by Alexander Long, an ML PhD who previously worked in Amazon's international machine learning group. The lab is backed by investors including Union Square Ventures and CoinFund.

labs.mission: Pluralis argues that frontier models should be trainable by open networks rather than by a few firms, and works on the compression and parallelism needed.

about: Polygl0t, also referred to as Project Polyglot, develops efficient language models for low-resource languages. It is funded by the German BMBF and the North Rhine-Westphalia ministry as part of TRA Sustainable Futures at the University of Bonn, and trains on Bonn's Marvin cluster and Jülich's JUPITER Booster.

Its Tucano models, first described in 2024, were trained on GigaVerbo, a corpus of about 200 billion deduplicated Portuguese tokens. The follow-up Tucano 2 paper of March 2026 introduces GigaVerbo-v2, with about 320 billion tokens, and models from roughly 0.5B to 3.7B parameters.
The group publishes weights, datasets and training code, including an LLM foundry repository and a fork of the evaluation harness.
labs.mission: Polygl0t aims to close the linguistic divide in NLP by making capable open models for languages that large developers serve poorly.

about: Preferred Networks was established in March 2014 as a spin-off from Preferred Infrastructure, founded in 2006. Toru Nishikawa is CEO and Daisuke Okanohara is COO.

In June 2015 the company released Chainer, an open-source deep learning framework that influenced dynamic-graph design; development ended in December 2019 as the team moved to PyTorch. It announced the MN-Core accelerator in December 2018, and the MN-3 system topped the Green500 list in June 2020.
Preferred Networks continues to publish open code and Japanese language models, including the PLaMo family.

labs.summary: Prime Intellect is a decentralized AI lab known for globally distributed training and RL tools, releasing models and code openly.

about: Prime Intellect was co-founded by Vincent Weisser and Johannes Hagemann. Its 2024 launch post framed the company around open, decentralized AI development.

In late 2024 it released INTELLECT-1, a 10B-class model trained on 1 trillion tokens across nodes on three continents with its PRIME distributed training framework, together with data and checkpoints. The company now offers inference, GPU compute, sandboxes and a model factory.

Its open-source projects include prime-rl, a framework for asynchronous reinforcement learning at scale, and the Verifiers library with an Environments Hub that lists thousands of community environments.
labs.mission: Prime Intellect pursues open, globally distributed AI development and wants individuals and small teams to be able to train and own capable models.

labs.tagline: The Princeton NLP group, source of SWE-bench, SimPO and Tree of Thoughts, with many open benchmarks, methods and models.
about: Princeton NLP is the natural language processing research group at Princeton University. Its GitHub organization hosts widely used research code and its Hugging Face organization hosts models and datasets.

The group's SWE-bench benchmark, published at ICLR 2024, tests whether language models can resolve real GitHub issues and became a standard evaluation for coding agents. SimPO, presented at NeurIPS 2024, is a reference-free preference optimization method, and Tree of Thoughts (NeurIPS 2023) is a deliberate problem-solving framework for language models.
Karthik Narasimhan is among the authors of SWE-bench; Danqi Chen also leads work in the group.
labs.mission: The group studies how language models learn, reason and act, and releases the resulting benchmarks, methods and code so that other researchers can reproduce and extend them.

about: Prior Labs was founded by Frank Hutter, Noah Hollmann and Sauraj Gambhir to commercialize TabPFN, a transformer pretrained on synthetic data that handles tabular prediction in a single forward pass.

about: Projecte Aina is a Catalan government initiative created by the Generalitat de Catalunya's digital policies department to ensure that Catalan is well supported in language technology. The Barcelona Supercomputing Center (BSC) carries out the technical work, with its Language Technologies Unit credited as author of the models.

The project has built a large Catalan text corpus, started a Catalan speech corpus and published models and datasets on Hugging Face under permissive licenses. Its Salamandra family of 2B, 7B and 40B models, released under Apache 2.0, was trained on the MareNostrum 5 supercomputer with Aina funding.
Resources are intended for reuse by companies, public bodies and researchers, and the project also runs community programs such as the Aina Challenge.
labs.mission: Aina aims to ensure that technology understands and speaks Catalan, with open resources that others can reuse.

about: Proxecto Nós was launched in 2020 by the Xunta de Galicia and entrusted to the University of Santiago de Compostela through CiTIUS and the Instituto da Lingua Galega (ILG). It aims to give Galician openly licensed resources and tools in intelligent technologies.

It produced CorpusNós, described as the largest openly available collection of Galician text, and the first generative language models focused on Galician, including the 1.3 billion parameter Carballo, adapted from Catalan-Spanish-English models of the Aina project. The project also operates public demonstrators for machine translation, speech synthesis, speech recognition and retrieval-augmented chat. CiTIUS was later selected to lead the Galician model in a Microsoft collaboration with BSC and HiTZ on models for Spain's official languages.
labs.mission: The project seeks to ensure Galician has the digital resources and AI technology needed for everyday use.

The architecture has gone through versions named Dove, Eagle, Finch and Goose. RWKV-7 Goose, described in a March 2025 arXiv paper, generalizes the delta rule with vector-valued gating and supports state tracking. Models of 0.4B, 1.5B and 2.9B were released under Apache 2.0.
Contributors come from EleutherAI, Recursal AI and several universities.
labs.mission: RWKV aims to offer an efficient alternative to transformers with linear-time inference.

labs.summary: Speech AI company that open-sourced the CSM-1B conversational speech model.
labs.tagline: A conversational speech company that open-sourced the CSM-1B base speech model while building voice companions.
about: Sesame builds conversational voice AI and is co-led by Brendan Iribe, a co-founder of Oculus, and Ankit Kumar. It announced its voice companions in February 2025 and has since pursued voice-driven wearables, raising 250 million dollars in a round led by Sequoia Capital in October 2025.

In March 2025 it open-sourced CSM-1B, a base speech generation model pairing a Llama backbone with an audio decoder that produces Mimi audio codes. The release is under Apache 2.0 with ethical use guidelines.

The open checkpoint is a base model that has not been fine-tuned to a specific voice; a fine-tuned version powers the company's demo. The technical post lists Johan Schalkwyk, Ankit Kumar, Dan Lyth, Sefik Emre Eskimez, Zack Hodari, Cinjon Resnick, Ramon Sanabria and Raven Jiang.
labs.mission: Sesame aims for natural, voice-based conversational AI and shares a base model with the community.

about: Språkbanken Text is a research and development unit at the University of Gothenburg, established in 1975 and among the world's oldest language technology units. It is now being renamed simply Språkbanken within a national infrastructure.

It takes part in CLARIN and HumInfra, and the national infrastructure is moving its news and data services to sprakbanken.se.
labs.mission: The unit develops and shares language data and tools so researchers and society can work with Swedish text.

labs.name: Stanford NLP Group
labs.summary: Academic research group releasing widely used open NLP software and datasets, including DSPy, CoreNLP, Stanza and GloVe.
labs.tagline: The Stanford NLP Group is a leading academic research group whose open software, including CoreNLP, GloVe, Stanza and DSPy, underpins much of modern language technology.
about: The Stanford NLP Group was started in 2000 by Christopher Manning, who held a joint appointment in linguistics and computer science. It grew to include faculty such as Dan Jurafsky, who arrived in 2004, and Percy Liang, who joined in 2012. The group is part of Stanford University and brings together linguists and computer scientists.

Its software history begins with the Stanford Parser, released as open source in December 2002, and the first unified CoreNLP package appeared on 1 November 2010. Later releases include GloVe word vectors, the Python library Stanza for many human languages, and the DSPy framework for programming rather than prompting language models.
The group publishes code, data and papers openly, and its GitHub organization is among the most widely used sources of NLP tooling for researchers, students and industry engineers.
labs.mission: To advance the computational understanding of human language and to share research software and datasets that others can build on.

about: Stockmark is a Japanese company focused on business information and language models. Its co-founder and CTO is Kosuke Arima, and its researchers publish models on Hugging Face under the stockmark organization.

Stockmark-100b is a 100-billion-parameter model pretrained from scratch on about 910 billion tokens of Japanese and English text and released under the MIT license. The company later released Stockmark-2-100B-Instruct and a multimodal Stockmark-2-VL-100B, both developed under Japan's GENIAC program.
The models target Japanese business use, with a stated focus on reducing hallucination in domain questions.
labs.mission: Stockmark aims to provide Japanese-first language models that companies can run and adapt, with open weights.

labs.name: Swallow LLM
labs.summary: LLM project led by the Okazaki and Yokota labs at the Institute of Science Tokyo, adapting open models for Japanese.
labs.tagline: Swallow is a Japanese LLM project at the Institute of Science Tokyo that continually pretrains open models to give them strong Japanese ability.
about: Swallow is led by researchers in the Okazaki and Yokota laboratories at the Institute of Science Tokyo, together with the National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology (AIST). Naoaki Okazaki leads the project and the pre-training corpus team, Rio Yokota leads LLM training, and Sakae Mizuki leads instruction tuning and evaluation.

The project adapts existing open models such as Llama, Mistral, Gemma, Qwen and gpt-oss to Japanese through continual pretraining and instruction tuning. Its model list runs from the first Swallow models to Llama 3.3 Swallow 70B, Qwen3 Swallow and GPT-OSS Swallow.
Weights are published on Hugging Face under the tokyotech-llm organization, and the project documents its corpus and evaluation work for the Japanese community.
labs.mission: Swallow aims to build and openly release Japanese large language models and the corpora and evaluation methods needed to improve them.

about: The Swiss AI Initiative started in December 2023, seeded with more than 10 million GPU hours on the Alps system run by CSCS and a CHF 20 million grant from the ETH Domain. It is run with the ETH AI Center and the EPFL AI Center, with Swisscom as strategic partner.

Its main output is Apertus, released on 2 September 2025 in 8B and 70B sizes under Apache 2.0. Apertus was trained on over 1,800 languages and designed to follow European copyright law, with an emphasis on transparency and auditability.
An Apertus 1.5 release is listed for July 2026.
labs.mission: The initiative aims to build transparent, sovereign foundation models for Switzerland and to share them with the wider research community.

about: Te Hiku Media, formally Te Reo Irirangi o Te Hiku o Te Ika, is an iwi radio and media organization in Kaitaia whose site dates its roots to 1991. It runs Te Hiku Tech, which builds tools for te reo Māori.

Its Kōrero Māori campaign collected labelled speech under the Kaitiakitanga License, which restricts use of the data to the benefit of Māori people. The organization reported a speech recognizer for te reo Māori built with DeepSpeech, with accuracy of about 92 percent.
All content on its site is covered by the same licence, and contributors retain ownership of their data.
labs.mission: Te Hiku Media aims to revitalize te reo Māori with technology that Māori communities own and control.

labs.tagline: TurkuNLP is the University of Turku's language technology group, known for FinBERT and, with Silo AI, the Poro and Viking models.
about: TurkuNLP is a group of about 30 researchers at the University of Turku, ranging from research assistants to professors. Its main topics are syntactic and semantic analysis of Finnish, large language models for Finnish and other languages, biomedical and clinical text mining, and the analysis of internet registers and genres.

The group's resources include FinBERT, WikiBERT, FinGPT and the Turku Dependency Treebank. With Silo AI's SiloGen it built the Poro and Viking models on the LUMI supercomputer; Viking, released in 2024 in 7B, 13B and 33B sizes, covers the Nordic languages, English and code under Apache 2.0.
TurkuNLP co-hosts an open monthly seminar on NLP and AI with Omni Language AI Research, and publishes its code and models on GitHub and Hugging Face.
labs.mission: The group aims to produce open language resources and models for Finnish and the Nordic languages.

labs.summary: San Francisco AI lab releasing open-weight models including Zonos text-to-speech and the Zamba hybrid language models, plus an EEG foundation model.
labs.tagline: Zyphra is an AI lab in Palo Alto releasing open-weight models, including the ZAYA1-8B reasoning mixture-of-experts model.
about: Zyphra says it was founded in 2020 and lists members in Palo Alto, London and Montreal. Dealroom names Krithik Puthalath and Danny Martinelli as founders.
It has released ZAYA1-8B, a reasoning-focused mixture-of-experts model trained on AMD Instinct MI300 GPUs, and demonstrated large-scale training on a full AMD stack.
labs.mission: Zyphra aims at full-stack, efficient AI models.

labs.name: ÚFAL
labs.summary: Institute of Formal and Applied Linguistics at Charles University, a long-standing NLP lab behind UDPipe, MorphoDiTa and Czech language models.
labs.tagline: ÚFAL is Charles University's Institute of Formal and Applied Linguistics, behind UDPipe and Czech treebanks.
about: ÚFAL was established in 1990 at the Faculty of Mathematics and Physics, continuing the Laboratory of Algebraic Linguistics active since the early 1960s.
It develops UDPipe, a trainable pipeline for tokenization, tagging, lemmatization and parsing under MPL 2.0, and the Prague Dependency Treebank family.
labs.mission: The institute advances computational linguistics and language resources.
